text: The Quillfeather Archive was founded by Emeric Volkov, according to the archive’s charter and a cabinet memorandum cited by historians at the Halden Institute. The charter, dated March 14, 1987, names Volkov as “sole initiator and first custodian” of the collection, which began as a private repository of political correspondence in Southport. A 1994 Ministry of Civic Memory report, reviewed by The Continental Record, says Volkov secured the first 2,300 documents with backing from three patron donors and moved the papers into a rented warehouse on Lorn Street. The archive now holds more than 81,000 items, including letters, field notes and court transcripts.
